name: Two-Control Cycle Obstructions to Convex Realizability
statement: For every even $m\geq4$, the class $D_m$ is a finite convex-treelike dismantlable ample class outside $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{amp}}$, and every proper nonempty pc-minor of $D_m$ belongs to $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{amp}}$. The $D_m$ form an infinite antichain. Within the restricted construction $C_2(G)$, avoidance is complete: $C_2(G)$ is realizable if and only if it has no conditioning minor isomorphic to a $D_m$.
proof: The full coefficient criterion for $C_2(G)$ is the strict system $t_v<t_w$ on every arc. A directed cycle makes it inconsistent. For $D_m$, projecting or zero-conditioning a private coordinate leaves the acyclic construction on a path; one-conditioning a private coordinate yields a reflected learning space; conditioning a control yields a reflected downset; and projecting a control admits direct witnesses for every row array. Hence all elementary proper nonempty minors are realizable, and pc-minor closure handles every proper minor. A shortest directed cycle in any oriented bipartite graph is chordless and even, and zero-conditioning all other private coordinates leaves the corresponding $D_m$.
comments: The partial designation is essential: completeness is proved only among classes of the form $C_2(G)$, not throughout the ambient finite convex-treelike class.
